column1: What role does traditional web development assign to the database?
column2: It treats the database as dumb storage with all intelligence delegated to application classes.
column3: Frameworks like Rails, Django, and Laravel all follow this storage-first pattern.

column1: What must happen when non-app code (e.g., shell scripts) needs to access data in traditional MVC?
column2: It must route through application classes since no validation or rules exist at the database level.
column3: Nothing else may access the DB directly without risking rule violations.

column1: What gets rewritten each time Sivers switches programming languages?
column2: Every language rewrite requires reimplementing all the data logic that lived in application models.
column3: Six rewrites across 15+ years: Perl, PHP, Rails, PHP, Ruby, JS.

column1: What makes the traditional database-plus-application-code system coupled?
column2: Intelligence is split across two systems that cannot function independently of each other.
column3: The DB is dumb; the app holds the rules — neither works alone.

column1: How does Rich Hickey define "complex" in his Simplicity Matters talk?
column2: Complex means many things tied together (interwoven) and is an objective property, not a subjective judgment.
column3: Traditional MVC is complex because DB and app code are interwoven.

column1: How does Rich Hickey define "simple" in contrast to complex?
column2: Simple means a single fold or one ingredient — the direct opposite of complex.
column3: A self-contained database with all data logic inside is simple.

column1: Why is an ORM an example of something "easy but complex"?
column2: It is easy to install and convenient to use yet it ties many concepts together in a way that is objectively complex.
column3: Easy and simple operate on different axes — they are unrelated.

column1: Why does Sivers consider OOP classes an unnecessary complication for data logic?
column2: Because information (a hash/map of strings) is inherently simple and hiding it behind an object layer adds complexity without benefit.
column3: JSON APIs return the same hash-of-strings format — even more reason to skip abstractions.

column1: What does a CHECK constraint on a PostgreSQL table guarantee?
column2: Every row must satisfy the boolean expression enforced by the database, not the application.
column3: Example: `check (length(name) > 0)` prevents empty names at the DB level.

column1: What happens when a row is deleted with ON DELETE CASCADE on a foreign key?
column2: The database automatically deletes all referencing rows in the child table without any application code.
column3: Deleting a person deletes all their tags automatically.

column1: What does the trigger in Sivers's example do before insert or update?
column2: It trims extra whitespace from the name and lowercases the email before the row is written.
column3: Decouples data hygiene from application logic entirely.

column1: How does the get_person function handle the case where an email already exists?
column2: It selects and returns the existing row atomically instead of inserting a duplicate.
column3: The function starts with `if not exists (select 1 from people where email = a_email)`.

column1: What does json_agg inside a PostgreSQL view accomplish?
column2: It aggregates multiple child rows into a JSON array nested inside the parent row.
column3: Eliminates all app-level JSON construction and serialization code.

column1: What is the return type of Sivers's API functions?
column2: A single JSON value via `out js json`, so the app calls `select js from function_name()` to retrieve it.
column3: No row mapping, no DTO conversion, no serializer configuration needed.

column1: How does the outside application code call a PostgreSQL API function?
column2: It runs `select js from function_name($1, $2)` via DB.exec_params and extracts the JSON result.
column3: The same calling pattern works for REST APIs and client libraries.

column1: How thin is the application code in Sivers's architecture?
column2: About 20 lines: a DB connection, a helper that invokes PG functions, and route mappings.
column3: The Sinatra REST API and the Ruby client library are both ~15-20 lines.

column1: What is the only code that changes when switching to a new programming language?
column2: The thin pass-through layer that maps external requests to PG API function calls.
column3: All data logic, validation, and JSON shaping stays untouched in the database.
